conventions.convention: The scalar field is real or complex; all scheme errors and operator bounds use the same Banach-space norm. Positive time steps form a sequence tending to zero, and powers start with Sν⁰ = I.

Consistency is the one-step defect divided by the time step, uniformly along each exact orbit over finite grid times, for every vector in a dense invariant linear subspace. Convergence is uniform over finite grid times for every vector in X. Both maxima include time zero.
DC is explicitly assumed for Lax equivalence, through uniform boundedness in the convergence-to-stability direction.
Grid restriction and reconstruction satisfy PνRν = I, and ker Pν is invariant under U(τν). The lift advances the reconstructed component by Qν and the complementary component by the exact semigroup.
The reconstruction comparison constants a,b > 0 and restriction bound P > 0 are independent of the scheme index; grid stability uses the declared grid norms.
The diagonal heat model uses c₀ with coordinates j ∈ N including zero, and multiplier exp(−j²t), so the zeroth coordinate is preserved.

load_bearing.statement: A common-space interface consists of a real or complex Banach space and a strongly continuous solution semigroup with finite-time operator bounds. Schemes are bounded linear steps with positive time steps tending to zero; consistency, stability, and convergence have the stated same-norm, finite-time quantifiers.
For bounded grid maps with PνRν = I and U(τν)(ker Pν) ⊆ ker Pν, the bounded common-space lift is Sν = RνQνPν + U(τν)(I − RνPν).

Assume DC. For a common-space IVP interface and bounded time-scheme family consistent on its dense invariant subspace, convergence on every finite time interval is equivalent to stability there, with all three notions measured in the same norm of X.
For either scalar field, U(t)x = (exp(−j²t)x_j) indexed by j ∈ N is a strongly continuous semigroup on the Banach space c₀, with operator norm at most 1 for every t ≥ 0.

For a finite-grid lift, if a,b,P > 0 are independent of ν and satisfy a‖g‖Gν ≤ ‖Rνg‖X ≤ b‖g‖Gν and ‖Pν‖ ≤ P, then common-space finite-time stability is equivalent to grid-update finite-time stability in the declared grid norms.
